title: Each Authoring command definition is reached by its one CLI command, MCP tool and route
when: Reads every command and query definition, whose identities are generated from Lathe's records, and Lathe's command records.
then: Expects each definition named by one CLI command, one MCP tool and one route, none shared, and every command of an aggregate with a slice defined.

title: Each Check command is run by name from the CLI, its MCP tool and its route
when: Runs `lathe check <command>`, the check_ tools and POST /api/check/<command>.
then: Expects each to run its one command, taking that command's fields.

title: Each Pattern following command is run by name from the CLI, its MCP tool and its route
when: Runs `lathe pattern-following <command>`, the pattern_following_ tools and POST /api/pattern-following/<command>.
then: Expects each to run its one command, taking that command's fields.

title: A command its aggregate refuses prints every reason with its rule, exits 1, and changes nothing
when: Runs aggregate commands the aggregates refuse from the CLI: an aggregate under a domain that does not exist, one whose ID is outside its domain, a link its relation does not allow and a record still referenced. Calls the same command's MCP tool.
then: Expects every reason printed with its rule, an exit code of 1 and the data files unchanged, and the tool to return the same refusal as data.

title: A refused Check command gives every reason and changes no file
when: Adds a check named like one of Lathe's, and changes and removes one of Lathe's own.
then: Expects each refused with its reason, naming lathe/data/check.jsonl, and no file changed.

title: A refused Pattern following command gives every reason and changes no file
when: Follows a pattern twice, gives a setting the pattern lacks, and a value with a reason too.
then: Expects each refused with its reason, and no file changed.

title: A refused command leaves the data and the files as they were
when: Applies three commands as one write (add a view, link it, add an automated test with no file), the last of which the store refuses.
then: Expects one problem with rule `check` on command 2, no trace of the view in the records or the database, and every data file unchanged.

title: A write checks the validation queries before any file changes
when: Sets a child entity's role to root, so its aggregate has two roots.
then: Expects the write refused by the `aggregate-root` validation query, naming the aggregate.

title: An add rewrites only its own table's file, sorted, with the ID registered
when: Adds a requirement.
then: Expects the add to report the table `uc_requirement` and the file `uc_requirement.jsonl`, the ID registered in `record_id` and `obligation` as a `uc_requirement`, only `uc_requirement.jsonl` changed, and the new row on line 2 with its columns in the table's order.

title: Writes run one after another, each on the state the one before left
when: Starts three adds at once.
then: Expects all three rows, in order, and a side connection that reads all of them.

title: A refused add names its rule and command: a key that exists, a bad parent, a link table
when: Adds a view with an ID in use, a view requirement under a view that does not exist, and a row straight into the `reads` link table.
then: Expects `primary-key` on command 0, `foreign-key` with the message `view_requirement TL-V09-R01: view_id "TL-V09" names no view`, and a `command` refusal that says to use link.

title: A row without a required field is refused
when: For each kind, loads its first row without each required column other than its ID and parent columns, then with each enum column set to `bogus`.
then: Expects a `required` refusal on line 1 saying `<kind>.<column> is required`, and a `column` refusal on line 1 saying the value `is not one of` the enum's values.

title: An entity's fields are rows of their own table under it, read back in position order, each naming its column when it has one
when: Loads entity fields written out of position order, one with an example and some with a column name.
then: The fields come back by position under their entity, each with its column name when it has one; no other kind carries field rows.

title: Each aggregate's commands change one aggregate through its repository, held to its rules, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Builds each aggregate's data set with its own Add commands, changes each kind, gives inputs of another shape, and runs commands as lathe <aggregate> with flags, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/<aggregate>/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only its aggregate's own tables, each refused one to name its rule and reason, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: Each Check and Product setting command changes one aggregate through its repository, held to its rules, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Builds the Check aggregate's data set with its own commands, changes each kind, gives inputs of another shape, and runs commands as lathe check with flags, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/check/<command>; does the same for the Product setting aggregate.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the aggregate's own tables, each refused one to name its rule and reason and change no file, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: Each Pattern following command changes one aggregate through its repository, held to its rules, and each interface runs the command it names
when: Builds the Pattern following aggregate's data set with its own commands, changes each kind, gives inputs of another shape, and runs commands as lathe pattern-following with flags, as their MCP tools and as POST /api/pattern-following/<command>.
then: Expects each accepted command to write only the aggregate's own tables, each refused one to name its rule and reason and change no file, and each interface to run the command it names.

title: The Aggregate tests start from the Aggregate's own data set, built with its own Add commands
when: Builds the Aggregate data set with the aggregate's own Add commands.
then: Expects the data set written and each aggregate read whole from it.

title: The Check tests start from the Check's own data set, built with its own Add command
when: Builds the Check data set with Add a check.
then: Expects the data set written and a check read whole from it.

title: The Pattern following tests start from its own data set, built with its own command
when: Builds the Pattern following data set with Follow a pattern.
then: Expects the data set written and a following read whole from it.

title: No stylesheet rule in Platform's shell uses display: contents or :has()

then: Expects no `display: contents` and no `:has()`. Then opens a record page and expects its Children section's Expand all inside the section's own header row.

title: A record page's Expand all sits in its own section's header row, laid out in the markup

then: Expects no `display: contents` and no `:has()`, and the Use cases section's own header row, with Expand all inside it when the button shows.

title: No selector in Platform's stylesheet names only elements, beyond the base styles

then: Expects each selector to name a class, attribute or ID, unless it names only base elements.

title: The exploring views' style rules select by class, attribute or ID
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` (not keyframe steps).
then: Expects each selector to name a class, attribute or ID, unless it names only base elements.

title: No style rule outside :root holds a hex, rgb() or hsl() color
when: Scans every style rule of `app/src/styles.css` outside `:root` for a hex, `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()` or `hsla()` value, and every component under `app/src` for an inline `style={{...}}` that holds a hex or `rgb()` color.
then: Expects no hex, `rgb()` or `hsl()` value in any style rule outside `:root`, and no color in a component's inline style.

title: No component of the exploring views sets a color in its inline style
when: Scans every `.tsx` component under `app/src` for an inline `style={{...}}` that holds a hex or `rgb()` color, after the same scan of `app/src/styles.css`'s rules outside `:root`.
then: Expects no hex, `rgb()` or `hsl()` value in any style rule outside `:root`, and no color in a component's inline style.

title: Generic components import only React, React DOM and each other
when: Reads every file in `app/src/components`.
then: Expects imports only from React, React DOM, the same folder and `../plural`.

title: Generic components import nothing of the spec pages, the graph or the data types
when: Reads every file in `app/src/components`.
then: Expects imports only from React, React DOM, the same folder and `../plural`.

title: Platform's code lowercases kind labels only through lowerLabel(), never toLowerCase()

then: Expects no template or sum that adds an "s" to a label. It also expects no label lowercased by hand with `toLowerCase()`.

title: The exploring views make kind labels plural only through plural(), never by adding an s
when: Reads the app's source, apart from `plural.ts`.
then: Expects no template or sum that adds an "s" to a label. It also expects no label lowercased by hand with `toLowerCase()`.

title: Every button and link of Platform's shell on the main pages has an accessible name
when: Opens the product list, a domain page, a record page and a record's graph.
then: Expects every visible button, link and form control to have an accessible name.

title: Every button, link and form control on the domain and record pages and the graph has an accessible name
when: Opens the product list, a domain page, a record page and a record's graph.
then: Expects every visible button, link and form control to have an accessible name.

title: Platform's code, the engine and the READMEs use American spelling
when: Reads the app and engine source, every data file and the READMEs.
then: Expects none of a list of British spellings (`aria-labelledby` excepted).

title: The exploring views' code and UI text, and every data file, use American spelling
when: Reads the app and engine source, every data file and the READMEs.
then: Expects none of a list of British spellings (`aria-labelledby` excepted).

title: Every grid in Platform's shell says its columns, a single column being minmax(0, 1fr)
when: Reads every style rule.
then: Expects each grid, other than a centering icon grid, to declare its columns.

title: Every grid on the exploring pages says its columns, so content shrinks with its panel
when: Reads every style rule.
then: Expects each grid, other than a centering icon grid, to declare its columns.

title: Each built-in theme's stylesheet sets only custom properties on :root and passes AA in both modes
when: Reads every built-in theme file.
then: Expects one theme file per built-in, each naming only `format`, `version`, `name`, `light`, `dark` and `tokens` and only tokens the stylesheet's `:root` defines; each theme's stylesheet to have only `:root[data-theme]` selectors and to set only custom properties and `color-scheme`; and ink, muted text and the accent at least 4.5:1 on paper and sheet for every built-in in both modes.

title: No built-in theme file names a token the stylesheet's :root does not define
when: Reads every built-in theme file.
then: Expects one theme file per built-in, each naming only `format`, `version`, `name`, `light`, `dark` and `tokens` and only tokens the stylesheet's `:root` defines; each theme's stylesheet to have only `:root[data-theme]` selectors and to set only custom properties and `color-scheme`; and ink, muted text and the accent at least 4.5:1 on paper and sheet for every built-in in both modes.

title: Only address.ts builds a record or group address in the app's and the desktop's source
when: Reads every source file in `app/src` and `desktop/src` except `address.ts`, parses addresses, and opens the products, a product, a domain, a record, a group on the Graph stage, Checks, the format and Appearance.
then: Expects no path built by hand under `/records`, `/specs` or `/graph`, nor a template starting `/${…}`; `/` the products, `DM`, `DM-SHOP` and `DM-SHOP-UC01` a product, domain or record page, and `/DM-SHOP/interaction-design/flow` a group; and on every page each in-app link to be `/` or start with an ID.

title: Every in-app link on the exploring pages is /, a lowercase app page or an ID
when: Reads every source file in `app/src` and `desktop/src` except `address.ts`, parses addresses, and opens the products, a product, a domain, a record, a group on the Graph stage, Checks, the format and Appearance.
then: Expects no path built by hand under `/records`, `/specs` or `/graph`, nor a template starting `/${…}`; `/` the products, `DM`, `DM-SHOP` and `DM-SHOP-UC01` a product, domain or record page, and `/DM-SHOP/interaction-design/flow` a group; and on every page each in-app link to be `/` or start with an ID.

title: No line of the app or the engine says legacy, redirect or alias
when: Reads every source file in `app/src` and `lathe/src`.
then: Expects no line that says legacy, redirect or alias, naming the file and line of each, and exactly one declaration of `addressOf`, taking the ID alone.

title: addressOf is declared once, taking the ID alone
when: Reads every source file in `app/src` and `lathe/src`.
then: Expects no line that says legacy, redirect or alias, naming the file and line of each, and exactly one declaration of `addressOf`, taking the ID alone.

title: knip finds no unused file, export or dependency in the app, the engine or the desktop app
when: Runs knip in `app/`, `lathe/` and `desktop/`, each with its own `knip.json`.
then: Expects it to report nothing.
notes: Also: T130 `unused-css.test.ts`, T131 and T132 `commands-and-icons-used.test.ts`, T133 and T134 `marks-have-meaning.test.tsx`

title: knip finds no unused file, export or dependency in the app, which holds the Explorer's code

then: Expects it to report nothing.

title: The Tab set's repository gives one value for a stale stored set, and React does not warn
when: Stores a tab set of another form, which the read drops from storage, then loads the Tab set twice and renders a component that reads it.
then: Expects both loads to be the same value and no getSnapshot warning on the console.

title: Every browser suite file takes its test from the shared one and stands in for the desktop only through the shared stand-in
when: Reads every file of the stability, accessibility and performance suites.
then: Expects none to import test or expect from Playwright itself, and none but the shared stand-in to set the desktop bridge.

title: The shared hover tokens are defined in :root
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` that sets a pointer cursor.
then: Expects a `:hover` rule naming the same class, and expects the shared hover tokens to be defined.

title: Every pointer-cursor rule has a :hover rule for the same class
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` that sets a pointer cursor.
then: Expects a `:hover` rule naming the same class, and expects the shared hover tokens to be defined.

title: The stage fills the window behind panels floating inset and frosted, each panel edge the one ResizeHandle
when: Reads the stylesheet and the source, and opens a use case on the Graph stage.
then: Expects the shell, inset, radius and floating surface and shadow tokens; no separator drawn outside ResizeHandle; exactly two splitters, the navigation's and the wiki card's, each a resize handle; the Graph stage filling the window behind and inside no panel; and the nav, wiki card, page bar and header strip each floating on its side.
notes: Also: `app/stability/panes.spec.ts`, which measures the panels and the stage in a browser.

title: On a record page the nav and the wiki card each resize by one handle at their edge
when: Reads the stylesheet's shell, inset, radius and float tokens and every component for a separator drawn outside `ResizeHandle`, then opens a use case's Graph stage with the wiki card open.
then: Expects the shell, gap and radius tokens, no separator drawn outside ResizeHandle, and on a record with the wiki and graph open the navigation's and the wiki card's edges as resize handles beside their panels.
notes: Also: `app/stability/panes.spec.ts`, which measures the panels and the stage in a browser.

title: One page bar holds the tabs, the one Stage switch and the wiki card toggle, and a stage's own tools float outside it
when: Opens a use case on the Graph and ERD stages, and on the Graph stage on a phone.
then: Expects one page bar, inside no panel or stage, holding in the desktop app the tab strip at its left (on a phone the Open pages button instead) and on the web no tabs, and at its right the one Stage group of `aria-pressed` buttons, one pressed, then the wiki card toggle last; no pane or pane header anywhere; the stage's own tools inside the stage, never in the page bar; the page's h1 in the header strip; and the page bar and header strip of fixed height.

title: On a use case, wide or on a phone, the page bar holds the page's controls and no stage tool
when: Opens a record alone, with the wiki and graph, and with both on a phone.
then: Expects one page bar, outside every pane, holding in the desktop app the tab strip at its left (on a phone, the Open pages button instead) and on the web no tabs, and at its right the one "View" group of `aria-pressed` toggles, one pressed per shown pane. On a wide screen each pane is a panel whose first child is its slim header: a non-interactive label naming its view, and only its close button (when more than one pane is open) and its full screen button, all icon buttons, with no tabs or groups in it. On a phone one pane shows, with no header. The title sits in the leftmost pane, and the stylesheet gives the page bar and the pane headers fixed heights.

title: Motion is shared and optional: every transition and animation uses the motion or hover tokens and is turned off under reduced motion
when: Reads every style rule in `app/src/styles.css` that sets a transition or animation.
then: Expects its times and easing to come from `--motion-speed`, `--motion-ease` or `--hover-speed`, and each such selector to be turned off by a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule or to apply only under `no-preference`. Expects the tokens to be defined, and code that animates frame by frame to take its timing from `readMotion()`, which reads them and checks `prefers-reduced-motion`.

title: The glide follows the shared easing: CSS's ease, read from the motion tokens
when: Compares the easing built from `MOTION_EASE` with CSS's `ease` curve walked finely, pans the camera halfway through its time, and parses motion tokens as the stylesheet writes them.
then: Expects the easing to match CSS's `ease` curve to four places, about `0.8024` at half time; a 300 px pan more than 60% of the way at half its time; `320ms`, `0.32s` and an empty value read as 320 ms; and `cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)` and `ease` parsed to the same curve, `linear` to a straight line.

title: The row link's ::after stretches over its row, with the row's other controls above it
when: Reads the style rules of `app/src/styles.css`.
then: Expects `.row-link::after` absolute with `inset: 0`, the `.record-list > li` tree rows `position: relative`, the rule for the row's other buttons, links and titled elements to set `position: relative` and `z-index: 1`, `.row-link:hover::after` to use `var(--hover-bg)` and `.row-link:focus-visible::after` an outline.

title: Every record row on the domain and record pages has exactly one row link to its record
when: Reads the style rules of `app/src/styles.css`.

title: Reloading brings back each tab's own stage
when: In the desktop app, opens a use case on the Graph stage, a view in a new tab on the Trace stage and an aggregate in a third, activates the first tab and reloads the app at its address.
then: Expects the same tabs in order with the same active tab, the address `?stage=graph`, the Graph stage drawn, and the second tab, activated, back on the Trace stage.

title: On a coarse pointer every clickable control of Platform's shell is at least 44 × 44 px
when: Reads `app/src/styles.css`.

title: On a coarse pointer every clickable control of the exploring pages is at least 44 × 44 px, a canvas's nodes by their laid-out size

title: The page bar, the header strip and every stage's toolbar each keep one height whatever their text

then: Expects the page bar and the header strip of fixed height, the strip one line whose title and counts are cut with an ellipsis, and every stage's toolbar never wrapping.

title: Stability: focusing anything moves the camera only, and no box changes its place or size

then: Expects each step stable, the camera different at each, and every box seen to keep the same place and size in the map throughout.

title: Every raw button outside Button.tsx is one of the allowed controls, in the source and on the pages

title: No paragraph on the main pages holds only a plain link: a standalone action is a button
when: Reads every `.tsx` and `.css` file under `app/src`, then opens the products, a product, a domain, a record, a record's Graph stage, Checks, the format and Appearance.

title: Accessibility: every page and state passes axe at WCAG 2.2 AA, at both widths, in every look
when: Opens each page and state (the products picker, the product, domain, record, interface and group pages, the Graph, ERD and Trace stages with the panels open and collapsed, Checks, the format and kind pages, Appearance, the record and add forms, quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, the chat, a tooltip, the nav drawer and the wiki card sheet) at 1440 px and 375 px, in Lathe and High contrast, light and dark, and under reduced transparency.

title: Accessibility: the Explorer's pages (domain, record, group, graph and ERD stage) pass axe at WCAG 2.2 AA, at both widths, in every look
when: Opens the Explorer's pages and states (the domain, record and group pages, and the Graph, ERD and Trace stages) at 1440 px and 375 px, in Lathe and High contrast, light and dark.
then: Expects axe-core to find nothing on each.

title: Performance: the app stays within its budgets on the production build
when: Builds the app for production; then, on a warm server, opens a record page three times, switches the stage from the Graph to the ERD and back, re-centers the graph three times at depth 3 in the Tree layout and in the Nested layout, and switches to the ERD stage a second time.
then: Expects the JavaScript that `index.html` loads at once (its scripts and module preloads) to be 250 KB or less gzipped; the median record page interactive within 1.5 s; each stage switch, and the second switch to the ERD, under 100 ms of main-thread work; each re-center under 500 ms of main-thread work, from the click until the glide has ended, with at most 3 frames over 20 ms and none of 100 ms or more. Prints the largest chunks and each re-center's work.

title: Only boxes in view and big enough are drawn, each with its label, with bars for the rest, within a budget
when: Frames the domain `P-D` in a 1000 by 800 view, then zooms all the way out.

title: In the Tree and Nested layouts, at every domain, stage and folder of every product, at depths 1 to 3 in two frames, siblings share one size and text scale and every drawn box shows its name

then: Expects the siblings in each map to be the same size with one text scale, every drawn box's label lines to give back its title and its kind and ID line, and the label to fit its box at its scale. On a failure it names the layout, focus, depth, frame, box and its size on screen.

title: Each label line is placed in map units at its face's size times its box's text scale, inside its box, and drawn at that size times the zoom
when: Builds the Tree and Nested maps of the test workspace and reads every box's label lines and badges.
then: Expects every box to have label lines, each line's size its face's (`TITLE_FONT`, or `META_FONT` when muted) times the box's text scale, each line wholly inside its box, and every badge inside its box's left, right and top edges.

title: In Platform's folder model a stage with one folder lists its records directly, and the folder has no address
when: Reads a domain's and a product's stages from the folder model and the graph's tree, unfolds a domain's Use cases in the nav, and opens the domain page, a domain with no capabilities and the skipped folder's address.
then: Expects Use cases (only capabilities) and Shared's Use cases (only patterns) to hold their records with no folder between, in the model, the tree, the nav and the domain page; Interaction design to keep its Flows and Endpoints folders; the empty one-folder stage to say Nothing yet; and the folder's address to name nothing.

title: On the exploring pages a stage with one folder shows its records directly in the nav, the graph's tree and the domain page
when: Reads a domain's and a product's stages from the folder model and the graph's tree, unfolds a domain's Use cases in the nav, and opens the domain page, a domain with no capabilities and the skipped folder's address.
then: Expects Use cases (only capabilities) and Shared's Use cases (only patterns) to hold their records with no folder between, in the model, the tree, the nav and the domain page; Interaction design to keep its Flows and Endpoints folders; the empty one-folder stage to say Nothing yet; and the folder's address to name nothing.

title: A trail of up to three places shows in full, and a longer one shows its first and last place around a labeled menu of the hidden levels
when: Collapses trails of three and five places, and renders the Breadcrumb with three places and then with five.
then: Expects three places shown as links with no button; with five, the first and last as links, each with its whole name as its tooltip and accessible name, and a "3 hidden levels" button that opens a "Hidden levels" list of the three hidden places as links, focus on the first, the arrow keys, Home and End moving through them, Escape closing it with focus back on the button, and a press elsewhere closing it.

title: The header strip, the wiki card and the phone's top bar draw their trails with the one Breadcrumb, and nothing else draws a trail
when: Opens a flow step on the Graph stage and reads the app's source.
then: Expects the header strip's and the wiki card's trails to be the breadcrumb, no component but `Breadcrumb.tsx` to draw a crumb, a graph trail or an up link, and the Breadcrumb used by exactly the phone's top bar, the header strip and the wiki card.

title: On a use case, a test and a term, each of the Graph, ERD and Trace stages draws something, with all three buttons enabled
when: Opens a use case, a test and a term on each of the three stages.
then: Expects the Stage group to hold Graph, ERD and Trace, none disabled, and the stage asked for to draw its graph, diagram or trace with some content, never the ERD's missing message.

title: On the Trace stage a record a row shows stands on its box, and any other record shows the product's rows
when: Opens on the Trace stage a UC requirement, a flow step, an entity and a term.
then: Expects the requirement's and the step's boxes focused in their rows with their paths lit, and for the entity and the term the product's rows drawn with nothing focused and the Trace button enabled.

title: Panels collapse for space wiki card first, then the nav, never the chat or a tool, and titles never break mid-word
when: Works out the panels collapsed for space at 1920, 1456, 1440, 1280 and 1024 px with every panel and the chat open, at 1440, 1280 and 1024 px without the chat, with a panel closed and with one held open, and reads every stylesheet.
then: Expects, with the chat and without it, nothing collapsed in a wide window, then the wiki card, then the card and the nav to its rail as the window narrows, the stage keeping 300 px at each width; a closed panel never counted; the chat and a tool over the stage never collapsed; a held wiki card making the nav give way; the card's CSS limits read from the shell's minimums; and no `word-break: break-all` and no title with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.

title: On a record page a narrow window collapses the wiki card, then the nav, each toggle saying so, and they come back as it widens
when: Opens a use case on the Graph stage in a 1000 px window, opens the wiki card from its toggle, then sets the window to 1920, 1000, 600 and back to 1920 px.
then: Expects the wiki card collapsed for space with its toggle saying so, the nav giving way once the card is opened anyway, every panel back at 1920 px with no toggle marked, the card and then the nav collapsing as the window narrows with the nav's remembered choice untouched, and every panel back at 1920 px.

title: The ERD map is laid out once: focusing two records moves no box, and the layout is read again for the same data
when: Asks for a product's ERD map and its layout twice on the same data and once on new data, then opens a domain on the ERD stage and focuses an aggregate by a click and an entity by Enter.
then: Expects the same map and layout for the same data, a new map laid out once for new data, and every box's place and size on the page the same before and after each focus.

title: The Trace stage is ordered once: focusing two rows moves only the camera and the fade, never a row
when: Switches a use case from the Graph to the Trace stage, then focuses another row's use case and a requirement of the first row.
then: Expects every box but the outcomes beside the focused row at the same place and size throughout, only the camera moving and the fade changing.

title: Every tool is an overlay in the address of the focus it is over, opened in order, closed topmost first, carried to a new focus, and counted in the open space
when: Applies address patches, reads the overlays of several queries, carries them to new addresses, parses the old full-screen addresses, works out the open space and crowding with a tool open, and reads the dialog and panel sources.
then: Expects each patch to replace its parameters at the end and drop empty ones, the topmost overlay to be the last opened, Escape's link to close it, a tool (never a format page) carried to a new focus, the old addresses to be no pages, a tool to shrink the open space and the wiki card to give way to it, and the dialogs and panels to share one focus hook.

title: Checks, Appearance, the theme editor, a format page and the products picker each open over the stage, which keeps its focus; Escape closes the topmost and focus returns
when: On a use case, opens Checks from the nav, a check's page from it, Appearance, the theme editor and quick open over Checks, pressing Escape after each; then opens the products picker.
then: Expects each tool floating at the left with the stage and its focus still there, the check's page in the wiki card, Escape closing the card's page, then the panel, focus back on the nav's Checks link, quick open closing alone before the panel, and the picker over the dimmed, inert stage of the last product, Escape going back to it.

title: The Graph, ERD and Trace stages show the same controls in the same order and places, folding them in one fixed order
when: On a use case, opens the Graph stage, then the ERD, then the Trace, and reads each stage's toolbar and camera; reads the toolbar's forms; then opens the Graph with a toolbar too narrow for the Changes controls and depth.
then: Expects one toolbar at the top of the open space on each, its step buttons Left, Right, Up, Down, Out and In then Frame first, the stage's own controls after them (Tidy up on the ERD, Expand row, Expand all and Tidy up on the Trace) and no Key; each step showing its arrow and letter; the camera's Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit the whole map in the corner, and no other zoom controls. Expects the forms, widest first, to hide the names and the baseline picker, then fold the Changes controls into More, then depth, then drop the step letters, and to fold the steps only in the last (the phone's), never Frame or the primary controls; and on the narrow Graph the steps with their letters, Frame, the layouts and the filters in the row, More at its end holding the Changes controls with the baseline picker, then depth.

title: On Lathe's own spec every node each stage draws is reached by keyboard from the product
when: Loads Lathe's spec with its chains, and from the product searches breadth first over every move of the walk (the four arrows, Out and In): on the Graph in each layout, on the ERD over its laid-out map, on the Trace over its rows.
then: Expects every box of the Graph's map in each layout, every region, aggregate area and entity of the ERD, and on the Trace every outcome and every row's use case and stage boxes reached, naming any that is not.

title: Adding a record moves only what it changed and keeps the camera, on the Graph, the Trace and the ERD
when: Frames a use case on the Graph's Tree, has an Agent add a requirement to it through the CLI, then on the Trace stage has an Agent add a use case and presses Tidy up. Then opens an aggregate on the ERD and has an Agent add an entity to it.
then: Expects on the Graph the new requirement among its siblings in ID order and every other box at its place and size; on the Trace the new use case's row drawn, every row shown before in its order and every box of the rows above the new one at its place, and Tidy up drawing every row with the focus's box where it was on screen; the camera unmoved on both stages. On the ERD, the new entity drawn, every box of the other domains at its place inside its region and its size, and the camera unmoved.

title: A change on the ERD moves only its aggregate's boundary or its domain's region
when: Lays out the model product's ERD, then adds, removes, renames and moves an entity and adds an aggregate, and lays it out again from the layout before; then tidies it up.
then: Expects every box outside the changed aggregate's boundary at its size and at its place inside its parent, unless a sibling that grew or moved now overlaps where it was, when it is pushed only right or down; no two siblings overlapping; nothing pushed by a box that shrank; the same layout again for unchanged data; Tidy up giving a first layout's picture; and each line drawn between its boxes as they glide.

title: The focused box is whole in the frame: a focus with many children, a box taller than the pane, a box at the map's edge or under a panel, on the Tree, Nested and Map
when: Frames Tree foci with two, eight and forty children at depths 1 to 3 in three panes; asks wholeIn for a box already whole, one at the map's edge cut by a panel at the left and the toolbar at the top, and one taller than the frame; frames a Map record too big for street level and a small one, and every box of a Nested map.
then: Expects every focus whole in the pane, its first child beside it; wholeIn to leave a whole box as it is, move a cut one in as little as it takes at the same zoom, and zoom a tall one out until it fits (from its top left corner at the least zoom); the Map's big record zoomed out whole and its small one at street level, and every Nested box whole.

title: On the Graph, the Trace and the ERD, the framed focus is whole and clear of every panel
when: Opens a pattern with twenty-three rules on the Graph's Tree at depths 1 to 3 with the minimap on, then in the Nested view and the Map; a use case with its flows on the Map and on the Trace stage; and a domain on the ERD; at 1440 by 900.
then: Expects the focused box as drawn inside the canvas and overlapping no floating panel (the nav, the wiki card, the key, the minimap) and no stage tool (the toolbar) on every stage.

title: A field's input follows its column's type
when: Renders the shared ColumnField for an enum, a whole number, a list of texts, a required and an optional true or false, and a line and a long text, and turns texts into values.
then: Expects a select, a number, a text area, a checkbox, a select, an input and a text area, each labeled and described by its column, and each text the value its column takes, a text not of its type left for the command to refuse.

title: A shared field input knows no kind
when: Reads the shared field inputs' file.
then: Expects it to import nothing of the specs, the aggregates' slices, the shell, the graph or the views, and to name no kind.

title: The record actions take only a known action and a record ID, and ask the window's engine for the data file
when: Accepts each action with a record ID. Run `npm --prefix desktop start` and open a record page. Choose Reveal in Finder: Finder shows the record's data file selected. Choose Open in editor: the file opens in the editor at the record's line. Choose Copy ID and paste it: the record's ID. Change the record's title in the editor and save: the page shows the new title within a second or two.
then: Refuses paths, unknown actions, lower-case and malformed IDs and extra keys; asks the window's engine (find-record-data-file) for the data file and takes only a full path to a .jsonl file, nothing when the engine refuses, has no such read or does not answer; and builds the native menu. It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: Open in editor uses VS Code by default, another known editor, the default app or a command of one's own
when: Reads settings with VS Code as the fallback, opens known editors by bundle ID on macOS and by command elsewhere, passes the file to a custom command as an argument and never in its text, and names the editor for the menu. Builds the menus and clicks Zed in File › Open Records In.
then: Expects VS Code when no valid editor is saved or a custom editor has no command; a known editor opened by its bundle ID through `/usr/bin/open -b` on macOS and by its command elsewhere, and the default app for `system`; a custom command run through `/bin/sh` with the file as `$1`, never in its text; and the menu names VS Code, Default App and the custom command's first word. Expects VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Default App and Edit Settings File…, VS Code checked, and Zed chosen.

title: Every record ID a page shows is a real link to that record
when: Opens every page in the list and reads each record ID shown in code on the page and in the Checks panel.
then: Expects each such ID inside an `<a href>` whose path is that record's own page, with more than 50 IDs checked.

title: Folded rows open by button or arrow keys and stay open after visiting another page
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.
notes: Proved in app/test/tree.test.tsx by the cases: Folded rows open by button or arrow keys and stay open after visiting another page; A record page's wiki lists its children one level deep.

title: A folded use case or aggregate keeps its count of records
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.

title: A record ID named in text does not appear in the graph
when: Opens `DM-PAY-UC01`, whose goal names `DM-SHOP-UC01` and `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, then Shopping's domain page with a description naming `DM-SHOP-UC01`.
then: Expects two links, `DM-SHOP-UC01` and `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, each titled with its record's title; no `DM-SHOP-UC01` link in the facts' Links out and no `DM-SHOP-UC01` node in the graph neighborhood; and the domain's description linking `DM-SHOP-UC01`.

title: IDs in code blocks, code with other text, links and longer IDs are not linked; a lone-ID code span is
when: Renders Markdown naming a record ID in a code span with other text, a code block, a link, a longer ID and a lone-ID code span, and links mentions in HTML with nothing to link.
then: Expects no links for IDs in code blocks, code spans with other text, links or longer IDs, a link around a code span holding one lone ID, and HTML left unchanged when there is nothing to link.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link: every record row on the domain and record pages has exactly one row link, stretched over the row
when: Opens Shopping's domain page and the record pages of `DM-SHOP-UC01` and `DM-SHOP-CMD01`.
then: Expects every row of every `record-list` (each tree item's own row, and each plain row) that holds a record link to have exactly one `row-link`, whose href is a record's page.

title: No page shows a relation code as a heading or label
when: Opens every record of a workspace with a record of each kind.
then: Expects no heading, field label, table header, legend, label or caption to read as a relation code ("satisfies", "proves", "depends on", "proves this"), and the graph's edge and key labels and the ERD stage's line titles to read the meta-model's labels.

title: The record page shows the ID, kind, title, text fields as Markdown, parent and children
when: Opens a use case.
then: Checks in the wiki card its ID, its kind badge in its stage's color, its goal rendered as Markdown and its child requirements, and its data file and parent link; then checks that Markdown in a text field is rendered.

title: The record page shows links out and in, grouped and named by their labels, each clickable
when: Opens UC requirement `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, then follows its Traceability link to the flow step `DM-SHOP-UC01-FL01-S01`. Then opens use case `DM-SHOP-UC01`, which follows `DM-PAT-AUDIT` and has a problem of its own.
then: Expects the requirement's Designed by (`DM-SHOP-CMD01`, `DM-SHOP-UC01-FL01`, `DM-SHOP-UC01-FL01-S01`, `DM-V01`), Built by (`DM-SHOP-CMD01-H`) and Proved by (`DM-SHOP-UC01-R01-T01`), its facts' kind and Links in links; then the step's page with Fulfills `DM-SHOP-UC01-R01`, Invokes `DM-SHOP-CMD01` and Happens in `DM-V01`, each a link in its facts. On the use case, its facts' Links out and Links in are exactly the links its record summary holds each way, and its Problems section's count equals its list's length and the problems the Problems read gives it.

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
when: Renders a text field holding a script, an image with an onerror handler and a javascript: link, and Markdown holding an iframe and an onclick.
then: Checks that none of them reaches the page or runs.

title: The record page lists every problem about the record
when: Opens a test whose file is missing, then a use case with no problems.
then: Checks that a test with a missing file shows its error and badge, and that a record with no problems says so.

title: A click on a row opens its record, and a click on its chevron or second link does what that control does
when: On Shopping's domain page, clicks a capability row's chevron, presses Left on its link, Cmd- and Ctrl-clicks the row and clicks its padding; then, with a followed pattern, clicks the pattern row's "followed by" use case link and its plain text.
then: Expects a click on `DM-SHOP-CAP01`'s chevron to unfold it and stay on the page, Left on its row link to fold it, Cmd- and Ctrl-clicks left to the browser with no navigation, and a plain click on the row's padding to open `/DM-SHOP-CAP01`; on a pattern row, a click on its followed by link `DM-SHOP-UC01` to open that use case, and a click on its plain text to open `/DM-PAT-AUDIT`.

title: Every record ID named in the text becomes a link to its record, with its title on hover
when: Renders Markdown naming `TL-LEND-DR01` twice and `TL-LEND-UC01` in a list, with their titles known.
then: Expects three `a.mention` links, each to its record's page with its title on hover (One loan at a time, Lend a tool), and the text otherwise unchanged.
notes: Proved in app/test/mentions.test.tsx by the cases: Every record ID named in the text becomes a link to its record, with its title on hover; A code span holding one lone record ID becomes a link, keeping its code style; A text field links the records of the space it names, never the record itself; On a record page the records a text field names are links that move within the app; A domain overview links the records its text names, and an ID inside a longer one only as the longer.

title: An ID-shaped token that names no record stays plain text
when: Finds the links in a use case's goal followed by its own ID, where the goal names a pattern, an invariant and an ID that is no record.
then: Expects a text field's links to be the records of the space it names, without the record's own ID, and an ID that is no record left as plain text.
notes: Proved in app/test/mentions.test.tsx by the cases: An ID-shaped token that names no record stays plain text; On a record page an unknown ID stays plain text.

title: Lists on group pages stay at ten rows
when: Gives aggregate `P-D-A3` 13 invariants and opens its Invariants group page.
then: Expects the Invariants (13) page to show a search box named "Filter invariants of P-D-A3/invariant".

title: A domain page opens one level deep, and Expand all opens the rest
when: On a domain page.
then: Expects use cases and aggregates folded with their counts, opens and closes a row by button and by the arrow keys (moving into it and back to its parent), uses Expand all, and expects open rows still open after visiting another page.
notes: Proved in app/test/tree.test.tsx by the cases: A domain page opens one level deep, and Expand all opens the rest; A product page lists its domains but none of their records.

title: A list of up to 10 items is plain; a longer one scrolls inside, with search, a count and a no-match message
when: Renders the long list with 10 and with 12 items.
then: Expects no search box at 10; at 12, a focusable scrolling region, a search box reached by Tab that filters by ID and by title, a count that follows it, a message when nothing matches, and Escape clearing the search.
notes: Proved in app/test/long-list.test.tsx by the cases: A list of up to 10 items is plain; a longer one scrolls inside, with search, a count and a no-match message; Every list in the spec pages stays at 10 rows and can be searched.

title: The wiki card's kind and each problem code link to their format pages
when: Opens a record page, a domain page, the Checks panel and a group page.
then: Expects the Kind row to link to the kind's page, each problem code to its check's page, and a group's kind to its page.

title: The Aggregate page reads its records through the Aggregate aggregate's own query
when: Opens the Aggregate aggregate's records: the aggregate and an entity.
then: Expects `GET /api/aggregate/get-aggregate?id=<ID>` among the requests and the record's text from the answer.

title: The Aggregate page writes only through the Aggregate aggregate's own commands, one per change
when: Edits an invariant and an entity, and adds a rule under an invariant with its suggested ID.
then: Expects exactly one command per action with only what changed and no generic write.

title: A record action opens the record's own data file, which the shell finds from its ID
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: In the desktop app, on a record, clicks Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in its facts, then right-clicks a record row, a graph node and the page title.
then: Finder shows the record's data file selected, the editor opens it at the record's line and the clipboard holds the record's ID; each right-click's native menu offers the same three, and each works.

title: The record actions take only a record ID, each on its own channel, and find the data file themselves
when: Sends the record actions with a known action and an ID, and with a path or an unknown action.
then: Expects only the known actions with an ID taken, and the data file found by the shell.
